## Legibility and limits

### Reader's final legibility assessment

The whole pages and both supplied halves were read in the first pass, with additional crops for cramped or cancelled passages; every page then received a second visual audit against its saved text. This does not eliminate the risk of plausible but mistaken readings in the fast handwriting. The least secure passages are the crowded revisions on 091–094, the small marginal word on 101, the DVR and pseudo-section proof revisions on 106–109, and especially the incidence argument and its warning on 122–124; the overwritten descent hypotheses and cancelled proof on 126–129 and the lower edge of 131 also warrant close checking.

The reused typescripts are generally more legible, but their black cancellations, added mathematical glyphs, typewriter letter/number ambiguities and incomplete formula slots remain risks. Scan 132 is particularly important: missing signs and unclosed visible punctuation are intentional features of this diplomatic text, not completed mathematics. The reading doubts are local confidence judgments, not a measured error rate; absence of a doubt mark should not be taken as a guarantee of correctness.

Nontextual figures, including marginal strokes and doodles, are manually drawn TikZ approximations of the visible geometry. No scan image, OCR output, or context-derived correction is embedded in the transcription. Mechanical brace and environment checks were performed; a full LaTeX compilation was not available because the installed TeX programs lacked their format/package data, as documented in `records/tex_environment_check.md`.

### Aggregated record summary

This aggregation covers 43 page records (scans 089, 090, 091, 092, 093, 094, 095, 096, 097, 099, 100, 101, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106, 107, 108, 109, 110, 111, 112, 113, 114, 115, 116, 117, 118, 119, 120, 121, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 127, 128, 129, 130, 131, 132) and 232 recorded doubt entries: 2 high, 81 medium, and 149 low confidence. These are recorded reading judgments, not an estimate of the transcription's error rate. No image was inspected by this aggregation script.

The least trusted entries in these records are those explicitly marked **low** confidence, on scans 089, 091, 092, 094, 097, 099, 100, 101, 102, 105, 107, 108, 109, 110, 111, 112, 114, 116, 117, 118, 119, 120, 121, 122, 123, 124, 126, 127, 128, 129, 130, 131, 132; the table preserves their exact locations and qualifications. Absence of a doubt entry is not a certification that a page is unambiguous.

The following recorded observations bear directly on orientation or legibility; they are reproduced verbatim:

- Scan 090: Supplied scan is upside down. All three images inspected after 180-degree rotation.
- Scan 091: Margin explicitly qualifies existence of B*; following words remain difficult.
- Scan 091: Diagram preserves visibly headless left and right strokes as dash arrows.
- Scan 093: Single cancelled typed salutation; remaining surface blank apart from pencil foliation and faint reverse-side show-through.
- Scan 095: All three supplied images viewed upright by 180-degree rotation.
- Scan 117: Reused annotated typescript on descent, physically upside down relative to archival number.
- Scan 118: Drawing and curving pen lines are reproduced; diagram has revised and heavily inked components.
- Scan 119: A non-effective descent example is attributed to Serre using Nagata’s nonprojective surface; dimension overwriting is uncertain.
- Scan 122: This is among the least secure pages, especially the incidence paragraph, slanted marginal note, and overwritten corollary number.
- Scan 126: Back-side show-through was not mistaken for live foreground text; whole and halves, top revision and condition (v) crops read.
